title: བར་དོ་ཐོས་གྲོལ་ཆེན་མོ།
titleEn: The Tibetan Book of the Dead — The blood-drinkers of days eight to eleven: Buddha, Vajra, Ratna and Padma Heruka
part: 10 · The blood-drinkers of days eight to eleven: Buddha, Vajra, Ratna and Padma Heruka
draftNote: Read from one blockprint at the resolution of an online scan; doubtful places are marked in the notes, and the text has not yet been collated with other prints.
source: Zab chos zhi khro dgongs pa rang grol las: Khro bo'i bar do 'char tshul bstan pa (the wrathful deities), pages 90–98 of the reproduction, from an undated Tibetan blockprint of the Thos grol cycle reproduced by the Buddhist Digital Resource Center as W23710 (text ga), read from the page images. It is a traditional blockprint, so no modern editor's work is involved. Two transcriptions found online, one of this print and one of another, were used to check the reading and are not the text. The page gives the print's wording and spelling. Three things are ours: the spaces between words, which Tibetan does not write; the line-end abbreviations, written out; and clear misprints corrected, each named in its note. Where another print reads differently in a way that matters, the note says so. Letters: the Wylie system (Extended Wylie for the Sanskrit words). Pronunciation: the reading style of central Tibet in the THL Simplified Phonetic Transcription (Germano and Tournadre, 2003), produced by rule from the spelling; a living reader's pronunciation will differ in places. The translation is new, made from the Tibetan. Still to do: the text has been read from one print at the resolution of an online scan, and doubtful places are marked in the notes; it has not been collated with the other blockprints.

sentences.l: This and Wearing-Liberation, two, proclaimed-by: gold's maṇḍala on turquoise's inlay arranged with alike-because, proclaiming do!
sentences.i: To proclaim the two together, this and the Liberation through Wearing, is like setting turquoise inlay on a golden maṇḍala: so proclaim them.
sentences.n: The part begins on the line where the last ended, after the praise of the Great Liberation through Hearing. 'di, 'this', is that book. Btags grol, 'Liberation through Wearing' (btags, the past stem of 'dogs, 'to tie on, attach'; grol, 'freed'), is the name of a companion text of the same cycle, mantras that free by being worn on the body; it is translated in the idiomatic line. gnyis, 'the two'. bsgrags pas, 'by proclaiming': bsgrags is the past stem of sgrog, 'to proclaim, to cry aloud' (sgrog / bsgrags / bsgrag / sgrogs). gser gyi maN+Dal, 'a golden maṇḍala', here the round plate of an offering, which is set with precious things; g.yu'i phra, 'inlay of turquoise' (phra, 'fine work, inlay'), is doubtful on the image ([?]): one stack with a pha-like body and a subscript r, where the other recension has 'phra. bkod pa, 'set, arranged'; dang 'dra bas, 'because it is like'. bsgrags par gyis shig, 'do the proclaiming!': gyis shig is the command 'do!', as in the parts before. The print runs dang and btags together across the line join (the nga ends against the frame), here divided.

sentences.l: Your before-at peaceful's between dawned though, recognition not seized-because, still here wandering must came-about is.
sentences.i: Earlier the peaceful bardo dawned for you, but you did not recognise it, and so you have had to wander here still.

'khyams pa dgos byung ba yin no, 'it has come about that you must wander' (003 has the same 'khyams dgos byung ba yin no of the first days): dgos, 'must, need'; byung, the past of 'byung, 'to happen'. dgos and byung are both marked doubtful ([?]) and are not in the other recension, which has only 'khyams pa yin no, 'you are wandering'; the reader saw them fairly clearly at twelve times enlargement, but a second reader has not confirmed them.

sentences.l: Now, as-for, day eighth on: blood-drinking wrathful-ones' deity-host dawning comes. Not distracted-way recognition seizing do!
sentences.i: Now on the eighth day the host of blood-drinking wrathful deities will dawn. Do not be distracted: recognise them.
sentences.n: zhag brgyad pa, 'the eighth day' (brgyad, 'eight', with -pa, which makes the ordinal), counting on from the seven days of the peaceful deities. khrag 'thung, 'blood-drinker' (Sanskrit heruka), as in 009. 'char du 'ong ngo, 'will come to dawn'. ngos zin par gyis shig, 'do the seizing of the face', recognise, as on the first day (003).

sentences.i: O child of noble family, the great and glorious Buddha Heruka, dark maroon in colour, with three heads, six arms and four legs spread wide,
sentences.n: The first of the five blood-drinkers, one for each buddha family; the description runs as a string of phrases, each closed by ༔ and most by -pa, 'being, having', down to the verb at the end of the sentence. dpal chen, 'great glorious' (dpal, 'glory'; chen, 'great'), a title of the herukas. Buddha he ru ka, Sanskrit in Tibetan letters, 'the heruka of the buddha family'; buddha is crushed against the frame at the line end and doubtful ([?]), though the other recension has the same name. zhes bya ba, 'so called'. smug nag, 'dark maroon' (smug, 'purplish brown'; nag, 'black'). dbu, 'head', phyag, 'hand, arm', and zhabs, 'foot, leg', are the respectful words. bsgrad[?] pa: the stack is taller than ga with ra and seems to carry an s on top; the other recension has bgrad pa, which the print itself has for the three herukas after this one; bgrad pa is 'spread wide, set apart', of legs planted in a wide stance, and the sense is the same either way. sentences.l: A-la-la and ha-ha's(?) loud-laughter sounding; sha'u(?) so-called and whistling's sound great sounding; head-hair red-yellow upward(?) streaming and blazing; sun-moon and, snake black and, skull-dry with(?) head-on adorned;
sentences.i: crying 'a la la!' and laughing aloud, 'ha ha!'; sounding the cry 'sha'u!' and a great whistling; his red-gold hair streaming upward and blazing; his head adorned with the sun and moon, black snakes and dry skulls;
sentences.n: a la la, a cry of joy or wonder; ha ha, the sound of laughter, here with -'i, 'of': ha ha'i is doubtful ([?]), for the reader sees no e-vowel where the other recension has ha he'i. gad rgyang, 'a far-carrying laugh' (gad, 'laugh'; rgyang, 'far'). sgrog pa, 'crying out, sounding', the present stem of the verb whose past is bsgrags in the first sentence. sha'u, a cry, is doubtful ([?]); the traces fit the other recension's sha'u. zhes pa, 'so called', 'the (sound) called'. bshugs is taken as 'whistling, hissing'; the other recension has bshug pa'i; the sense is not sure. dbu skra, 'hair of the head' (respectful); dmar ser, 'red-yellow', orange or tawny. gyen du, 'upward': du is doubtful ([?]), and the print runs it and 'phyo together across the line join, here divided. 'phyo, 'to stream, to fly in the wind'. dbur, 'on the head' (dbu with -r). thod skam, 'dry skull' (thod, 'skull'; skam, 'dry'); kyi, 'of', where kyis, 'by, with', is meant (the other recension has gyis); the print is kept and read so. The other recension has here two phrases: the sun, moon and dry skulls adorn the head, and the black snakes and fresh skulls (thod rlon) the body; the print puts all three on the head and has no fresh skulls.

sentences.l: Hands six, right's first in wheel; middle in axe; last in sword; left's first in bell; middle in plough; last [ … ] holding,
sentences.i: in his six hands, on the right, the first holds a wheel, the middle an axe, the last a sword; on the left, the first a bell, the middle a plough, and the last [an implement the scan does not show];
sentences.n: dang po na, 'in the first'; bar pa, 'the middle one'; tha ma, 'the last': the six hands are counted on each side from the top. 'khor lo, 'wheel'; dgra sta, 'axe' (dgra, 'enemy'; sta, 'axe'); ral gri, 'sword'; dril bu, 'bell'; thong gshol, 'plough'. bar ba is the print's spelling of bar pa. Two places on this line cannot be filled. (1) After bar ba na the print has an uninked blank about the width of a word, where the other recension has bhan dha, 'skull-cup', in the middle left hand. A word was probably erased from the block or never cut: nothing is printed, so nothing is written. (2) After tha ma two stacks stand where the name of the implement in the last left hand should be, and they cannot be read in the scan, even enlarged ten times: the first is a ka- or kha-like letter with something below it, the second has a head like Ta over a curled subscript. They are left out of the text, which reads tha ma bsnams par. A khaṭvāṅga (khaTwaM, the staff topped with skulls) is possible, but it is not confirmed, and the other recension gives no candidate, for its item for the last hand, thong gshol, already stands in the print in the middle hand. bsnams par, 'holding', the respectful word: with -r it runs on to the next phrases.

sentences.i: with a clacking of the tongue and a roar as loud as thunder; the fire of wisdom blazing from between his hairs, which blaze like vajras; sitting with one leg stretched out and one drawn in on a seat borne up by a garuḍa: so he dawns from the east of your own brain, before your very eyes.
sentences.n: rkan sgra, 'the sound of the palate', a clicking or clacking made with the tongue; thug chom is taken as a word for that sound; the sense is not sure. 'ur sgra, 'a din, a roar' (008). 'brug ldir ba tsam pa, 'as much as the booming of thunder' (008): the print has no verb after it; the other recension has tsam sgrog pa, 'sounding as loud as', and the print's tsam pa, 'being as much as', is kept and read so. rdo rje 'bar ba'i spu seb nas, 'from between the hairs blazing (like) vajras': spu, 'hair of the body'; seb is the print's spelling of gseb, 'gap, midst', which the other recension has; rdo rje 'bar ba'i may also be read 'of the blazing vajra', the body. ye shes kyi me, 'the fire of wisdom'. khyung, 'garuḍa', the great bird; gis, 'by', is doubtful ([?]): a narrow trace stands between gi and the next letter. btegs pa'i, 'lifted', the past stem of 'degs, 'to lift', where the other recension has the present 'degs. brkyang bskum du, 'stretched and drawn in', one leg out and one bent; bzhugs par, 'sitting', the respectful word, with -r running on to the verb. klad pa, 'brain'; shar, here 'east', as lho, 'south', and nub, 'west', in the days after. 'char ro, 'dawns', with the sentence-ending -o after -r. The print runs gi and mngon together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.n: zhal sbyor, 'joining of faces', union: sbyor, 'to join', is the present stem of the verb whose past is the sbyar of zhal sbyar in 004; the other recension has zhal sbyor ba. mngon sum du, 'manifestly, before one's eyes'. nub nas, 'from the west', the quarter of the lotus family; the other recension has klad pa'i nang gi nub nas thon rang la 'char du 'ong pas, 'emerge from the west within the brain and dawn to you'. de la ma dngangs shig repeats de la, 'at him'. dga' ba bsgom shig, 'meditate on joy!': dga' ba, 'joy'; bsgom, the future stem of sgom, 'to meditate' (sgom / bsgoms / bsgom / sgoms), taking shig for the command. The other recension has dran pa bskyed cig, 'rouse mindfulness', here. The print runs pa'i and nub together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.l: Own's knowing's body-as face-knowing do! Own's yidam's deity is-because, not be-afraid!
sentences.i: Recognise him as the form of your own awareness. He is your own yidam deity, so do not be afraid.

sentences.i: In truth he is the Blessed One Amitābha himself with his consort, so have devotion. Recognising and freedom come at one and the same time.
sentences.n: Padma Heruka is Amitābha (Snang ba mtha' yas, 'Boundless Light'), the buddha of the fourth day (005). The print runs mos and pa together across the line join, here divided.

sentences.l: So proclaimed-because: yidam's deity being-as face-knowing, then, two-as without-ly dissolving, then, buddha becomes.
sentences.i: When this is proclaimed, he recognises him as his yidam deity, dissolves into him without duality, and becomes a buddha.
sentences.n: yi dam gyi lha yin par ngo shes, 'recognises that he is the yidam deity', as in 009, where the days before had yi dam du, 'as the yidam'. ngo is doubtful ([?]): no naro is seen over the nga, though the e-stroke of the next syllable runs over it and may hide it; ngo shes, 'recognise', is the only sense, and the line above has a clear ngo shes. The print runs nas and sangs together across the line join, here divided. The next part begins on the same line, with the twelfth day: yang de ltar ngo sprad kyang.

glossary.ཞལ་དུ: zhal du — to the mouth, to the face (zhal 'face, mouth', the respectful word, + -du 'to')
glossary.ཞལ་སྦྱོར: zhal sbyor — union, the joining of faces (zhal 'face', the respectful word, + sbyor, the present stem of sbyor 'to join' (sbyor / sbyar / sbyar / sbyor)); said of a buddha and consort in union; beside zhal sbyar, with the past stem
glossary.ཞི་བའི: zhi ba'i — of the peaceful, peaceful (zhi ba 'peaceful' + -'i 'of')
glossary.ཞིང: zhing — and, while: links one verb to the next (zhing, the form used after a vowel and after ng, n, m, r, l, '; also cing, shing) · realm, field; a buddha-field (zhing, short for zhing khams): dag pa'i zhing 'pure realm'
glossary.ཞེས: zhes — so, thus: closes a quotation or a name (like inverted commas)
glossary.ཞེས་པ: zhes pa — so called, what is called (zhes 'thus, so', closing a name or a quotation, + -pa)
glossary.ཟངས་ཡག་ཏུ: zangs yag tu — perhaps 'with a copper gleam' (uncertain): zangs 'copper' + yag 'good, fine' + -tu 'as, with'
glossary.ཟིན་པར: zin par — seizing, holding (zin + -par): zin par the tshom med 'no doubt that (they) will seize it' · caught, held (zin pa + -r): mi zin par 'without being caught'
glossary.ཟིན་པས: zin pas — because (it) was seized, held (zin, the intransitive verb beside 'dzin 'to hold', + -pas 'because'): ngos ma zin pas 'because you did not recognise'
glossary.འཁོར་ལོ: 'khor lo — wheel ('khor lo); the wheel of the teaching
glossary.འཁྱུད: 'khyud — to embrace, hold in the arms ('khyud)
glossary.འགྱུར་རོ: 'gyur ro — becomes, will become ('gyur 'to become, to change' + the sentence-ending -ro)
glossary.འཆར་དུ: 'char du — to dawn, to arise ('char 'dawn, arise' + -du 'to'): 'char du 'ong 'will dawn'
glossary.འཆར་ཚུལ: 'char tshul — the way of dawning, how a thing dawns ('char 'dawn, arise' + tshul 'manner, way')
glossary.འཇིགས་པའི: 'jigs pa'i — of fear, fearful, terrifying ('jigs pa 'fear' + -'i 'of')
glossary.འཇིགས་ཤིག: 'jigs shig — be afraid! ('jigs 'fear' + shig, which marks a command); ma 'jigs shig 'do not be afraid'
glossary.འདི་སྐད་དོ: 'di skad do — these words (are said) ('di 'this' + skad 'speech' + the sentence-ending -do)
glossary.འདིར: 'dir — here, in this ('di + -r 'in') · in 'dir btsam du, as printed, perhaps for ldir 'roaring' (ldir ba tsam du 'as loud as the roaring of'); a guess
glossary.འདྲ་བས: 'dra bas — because it is like, being like ('dra ba 'alike, similar' + -s 'because')
glossary.འཕྱོ: 'phyo — to stream, fly loose in the wind ('phyo)
glossary.འཕྲོད: 'phrod — to meet, to be received (ngo 'phrod: 'the face is met', to recognise)
glossary.འབར་བའི: 'bar ba'i — of the blazing, blazing ('bar 'to blaze' + -ba + -'i 'of')
glossary.འུར་སྒྲ: 'ur sgra — din, roar ('ur sgra 'a sound of roaring')
glossary.འོང་བས: 'ong bas — because it comes, since it will come ('ong 'come' + -bas, the print's spelling of -pas 'because')
glossary.ཡང: yang — also, even, though (written kyang after g, d, b, s) · again, once more, at the head of a sentence (yang ngo sprad pa ni 'and the pointing out again')
glossary.ཡབ: yab — father (yab, respectful); the male of a buddha and his consort
glossary.ཡབ་ཡུམ: yab yum — father and mother; a buddha and his consort in union (yab 'father' + yum 'mother')
glossary.ཡི་དམ: yi dam — yidam, one's chosen deity (yi dam)
glossary.ཡི་དམ་དུ: yi dam du — as the yidam (yi dam 'one's chosen deity' + -du 'as, to')
glossary.ཡིན་ནོ: yin no — is, are (yin 'to be' + the sentence-ending -no)
glossary.ཡིན་པར: yin par — that it is, as being (yin pa 'being' + -r 'as, that'): X yin par shes 'know that it is X'
glossary.ཡུམ: yum — mother; a buddha's female partner, consort (yum)
glossary.ཡེ་ཤེས: ye shes — wisdom, primordial knowing (ye 'from the first' + shes 'know'; Sanskrit jñāna)
glossary.ཡེངས་པར: yengs par — distractedly, in distraction (yengs pa 'to be distracted' + -r): ma yengs par 'undistracted'
glossary.ཡོད་པ: yod pa — having, there being; one who has (yod 'there is' + -pa)
glossary.རཏྣ་ཀྲོ་ཏི་ཤྭ་རི་མ: ratna kro ti shwa ri ma — Ratnakrodhīśvarī, 'Wrathful Lady of the jewel family' (Sanskrit ratna + krodhī 'wrathful', written kro ti, + īśvarī 'sovereign lady', in Tibetan letters, with the Tibetan feminine -ma)
glossary.རཏྣ་ཧེ་རུ་ཀ: ratna he ru ka — Ratna Heruka, 'the blood-drinker of the jewel family' (Sanskrit ratna 'jewel' + heruka, in Tibetan letters)
glossary.རབ: rab — best, highest · very, intensely, before a verb or adjective (rab 'bar ba 'blazing intensely')
glossary.རིག་པའི: rig pa'i — of knowing, of awareness (rig pa 'knowing' + -'i 'of')
glossary.རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ: rigs kyi bu — child of the family, child of noble family (rigs 'family' + kyi 'of' + bu 'son, child'; Sanskrit kulaputra)
glossary.རིན་ཆེན་འབྱུང་ལྡན: rin chen 'byung ldan — Source of Jewels (rin chen 'jewel, precious thing' + 'byung ldan 'having arising'; Sanskrit Ratnasambhava): the buddha of the south and of the third day
glossary.རིན་པོ་ཆེ: rin po che — precious, a precious thing, jewel (rin 'value' + po + che 'great')
glossary.རིན་པོ་ཆེའི: rin po che'i — of the jewel, of the precious (rin po che 'jewel, precious thing' + -'i 'of')
glossary.རྐན་སྒྲ: rkan sgra — palate sound, a clicking made with the tongue (rkan 'palate' + sgra 'sound')
glossary.རྔེ: rnge — perhaps for rnge'u, a small drum (uncertain; the word as printed is not known)
glossary.རྡོ་རྗེ: rdo rje — vajra, the diamond-thunderbolt held by deities, emblem of what cannot be broken (rdo rje)
glossary.རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའ: rdo rje sems dpa' — Vajrasattva, 'Vajra Being' (rdo rje 'vajra' + sems dpa' 'hero of mind'; Sanskrit vajrasattva): the buddha of the second day, here the same figure as Akṣobhya
glossary.རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད: rnam par snang mdzad — Vairocana, 'He Who Makes Appear in Every Way' (rnam par 'in every way' + snang 'appear' + mdzad, respectful 'do, make'); the buddha of the centre
glossary.རྣམས: rnams — plural marker, set after the noun and its adjectives
glossary.ལ: la — to, at, in, for; after a verb or adjective: 'and' · among (… kyi rigs la 'among those of the … kind') · on (… la bzhugs 'seated on …') · from, of, with verbs of fleeing and fearing (X la bros 'flee from X')
glossary.ལན: lan — time, occasion (lan gsum: three times); also 'answer'
glossary.ལས་སྒྲིབ: las sgrib — karmic obscuration, the veil that one's past deeds lay on the mind (las 'deed, karma' + sgrib 'obscuration')
glossary.ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་སྐུར: longs spyod rdzogs pa'i skur — as the body of perfect enjoyment (longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku + -r 'as')
glossary.ལྡིར་བ: ldir ba — roaring, booming (ldir ba, from ldir 'to boom, roar'): ldir ba tsam 'as much as roaring'
glossary.ལྷ་ཚོགས: lha tshogs — host of deities (lha 'god' + tshogs 'host, gathering')
glossary.ཤའུ: sha'u — sha'u: a shouted cry (uncertain reading)
glossary.ཤར: shar — arisen, appeared (shar, past of 'char 'arise') · the east (shar): dkyil 'khor de'i shar nas 'from the east of that maṇḍala'
glossary.ཤེས: shes — to know, to recognise (shes); ngo shes 'recognise, know the face'
glossary.ཤེས་པ: shes pa — knowing; awareness, consciousness (shes 'know' + pa)
glossary.སངས་རྒྱས་པར: sangs rgyas par — to being a buddha, as a buddha (sangs rgyas 'buddha' + -pa + -r 'to'): sangs rgyas par 'gyur 'become a buddha'
glossary.སྐུ་མདོག: sku mdog — body colour, colour of a buddha or deity (sku 'body' + mdog 'colour'), the respectful word
glossary.སྐུར: skur — as the body, in the body of (sku 'body' + -r 'as, in')
glossary.སྐྱེས: skyes — arisen, born (skyes, past of skye 'be born, arise')
glossary.སྐྲག་ཅིག: skrag cig — be frightened! (skrag + cig, which marks a command); ma skrag cig 'do not be frightened'
glossary.སྒྲོག་པ: sgrog pa — crying out, sounding (sgrog, the present stem of sgrog 'to proclaim, cry aloud' (past bsgrags), + -pa)
glossary.སྔོན: sngon — blue (sngon, as in sngon po)
glossary.སྟེ: ste — and, namely: a linking word after a verb or a statement, leading on to what follows (also te, de)
glossary.སྟོབ་པ: stob pa — perhaps giving to eat, feeding (stob + -pa; the sense is not sure)
glossary.སྡང་མིག་ཏུ: sdang mig tu — with a glare, glaringly (sdang 'hatred' + mig 'eye' + -tu 'as, with')
glossary.སྣང་བ་མཐའ་ཡས: snang ba mtha' yas — Boundless Appearance, Boundless Light: the buddha Amitābha (snang ba 'appearance, light' + mtha' yas 'without limit')
glossary.སྤུ་སེབ: spu seb — the gaps between body hairs (spu 'body hair' + seb, the print's spelling of gseb 'gap, midst'; uncertain)
glossary.སྨུག་ནག: smug nag — dark maroon (smug 'purplish brown' + nag 'black')
glossary.སྨུག་ནག་ཏུ: smug nag tu — in dark maroon, as dark maroon (smug nag + -tu 'as, in'): smug nag tu yod pa 'being dark maroon'
glossary.ཧ་ཧའི: ha ha'i — of 'ha ha', the sound of laughter (ha ha + -'i 'of'; the reading is doubtful, perhaps for ha he'i)
glossary.ཨ་ལ་ལ: a la la — a la la: a cry of delight or wonder, a laughing exclamation

about: The second part of text ga, the bardo of the wrathful deities: days eight to eleven. It opens by joining this book to its companion, the Liberation through Wearing: to proclaim the two together is like setting turquoise on gold. Then the dead person is told that, because he did not recognise the peaceful bardo, he has had to wander on, and that the blood-drinking wrathful deities now dawn. On the eighth day comes Buddha Heruka, dark maroon, with three heads, six arms and four legs spread wide, blazing, laughing and roaring, his hands holding a wheel, an axe, a sword, a bell, a plough and an implement the scan does not show, embraced by his consort Buddhakrodhīśvarī; he dawns from the east of the dead person's own brain. He is not to be feared: he is the dead person's own yidam, and in truth Vairocana with his consort, and to recognise him is to be freed. Those who flee in terror meet, on the ninth day, Vajra Heruka, who is Vajrasattva; on the tenth, Ratna Heruka, who is Ratnasambhava; on the eleventh, after those whose bad habits make them see the deities as Lords of Death, Padma Heruka, who is Amitābha. Each has his colour, his six implements and his consort, and dawns from a quarter of the dead person's brain; each time nearly the same words are spoken: do not fear, recognise him as the form of your own awareness, and recognising and freedom come at once.
